Definition: to tread down, i.e. subjugate; specifically, to crumble off
BiblicalUsage: Radah is to tread down, to rule, to have dominion. God gave man dominion over the fish of the sea and the fowl of the air and every living thing that moveth upon the earth; He blessed them and said, 'have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air'; and the psalm says of the king, 'He shall have dominion also from sea to sea, and from the river unto the ends of the earth.'
TheologicalSignificance: The point for me is that dominion is a gift before it is a task: God gave man rule because He made man in His image, and the rule was meant to look like His — tending, not crushing. And I hold that the psalm's king shows what dominion is for: a king who rules from sea to sea so that the poor are delivered and the needy are saved.
